idea.description: Train the corrected NextItNet using target-matched stochastic recent-suffix inputs and moderate multiple-negative cross-entropy. Keep one jointly trained network and one selected checkpoint per category. The proposal explicitly targets broad relevance outranking specific recent matches and stale interactions persisting despite coherent recent behavior; it also targets Electronics’ weak sampled positive-negative separation. A matched full-context control distinguishes removing context from changing which historical targets receive supervision.
idea.motivation: Early research progress favors a modest training intervention over additional convolution branches or timestamp-dependent architecture. Suffix augmentation tests whether available historical context contributes to two observed user-facing failures, while multiple-negative classification tests discrimination against several alternatives. The original proposal confounded cropping with recency-weighted supervision: masking losses at removed positions changes target frequencies even when retained outputs cannot access the removed context. Matching target masks resolves that confound. These mechanisms remain hypotheses; the supplied diagnostics neither identify obsolete intent nor demonstrate that context removal will improve ranking. Missing compatibility and purchase-need information limits what this method can resolve.
idea.implementation_notes:
Starting point and invariants: use the supplied corrected baseline without inventing its architecture, optimizer or checkpoint rule. Preserve NextItNet, causal masking, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), family-specific sample_batch and ModelView. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, baseline optimizer and validation schedule, single-GPU execution, all four category routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Do not inspect other trials or their checkpoints. No execution, validation gain or diagnostic outcome is asserted here.

Experimental design: before execution, declare the configurations, checkpoint rule, stopping rule, evaluation schedule and allocations within 43,200 shared GPU-seconds, including diagnostics and failures. Retain the original unchanged reference. The four controlled configurations cross full versus cropped context with baseline versus multiple-negative loss; all four share the same suffix-derived target mask. Thus the full-context/baseline-loss configuration is the recency-weighted-supervision control, and cropped/baseline-loss corresponds to suffix-only training. Full-context/multiple-negative and cropped/multiple-negative distinguish the objective effect and its interaction with context removal. If projected costs prevent all configurations, prioritize the matched full-context versus cropped-context comparison under the baseline loss, retain the reference when feasible, and explicitly report omitted objective contrasts. Do not infer separate component benefits from an isolated combined run. Comparisons involve separately trained models, never fused predictions.

Target and context construction: use the baseline batch's chronological nonpadding sequence and original next-item targets. For each row with n valid input positions, keep the entire sequence with probability 0.5; otherwise draw suffix length uniformly from 1 through n. Construct a target mask retaining only originally valid target positions associated with retained input positions. Preserve repeated interaction events and repeated positive targets. In cropped-context configurations, zero preceding input positions; in matched full-context configurations, retain the complete original input but apply exactly the same target mask. Never shift or reconstruct targets after cropping. Keep left padding, mask padding throughout temporal operations, and use only causal, position-local transformations. Determine masks from inputs and dedicated training randomness, without validation/test information.

Matching and normalization: separate deterministic training RNG streams, all derived from seed 42, for batches, suffix masks, negative ranks and model stochasticity. Key batches, masks and negative samples by category, update, row and target position so variant-specific RNG consumption cannot change their identities. Predeclare this schedule before validation. For each controlled comparison, use the same target identities, target weights, negative identities and optimizer-update count. Average losses over retained valid targets across the batch, with unit target weights; report retained-target counts and their distribution by history length and position. Resample batches with no usable target rather than taking an empty mean. Keep the reference's original loss reduction and identify it as a practical baseline rather than the target-matched causal contrast. Dropout realizations need not match across architectures, but its probability and seed policy must remain fixed.

Receptive-field checks: compute R = 1 + sum_l((k_l - 1) * d_l), counting every stride-one temporal convolution on the longest path of the actual corrected architecture. Verify that there are no global sequence features or sequence-wide normalization invalidating this calculation. For each retained target, record whether cropping removed any valid input within its receptive field and how many. Context removal outside that field cannot change its deterministic evaluation-mode output. Do not interpret unchanged outputs as evidence that the model learned to ignore stale interests. Training dropout can change individual stochastic realizations.

Negative sampling: start with at most eight unique uniform negatives per retained target and temperature 1.0. Define each user's exclusion set as their complete training-item set, including events later than the current training position; deduplicate this set only. This is explicitly training-wide exclusion rather than prefix-only exclusion. Repeated items remain legitimate positive targets and are never negatives. Exclude padding and the current target explicitly as safeguards. Never use validation or test labels for exclusions. Record the catalog convention, exclusion policy, per-position sampling scope, RNG specification, negative counts, temperature and reduction.

Rejection-free sampling: map catalog IDs 1..N to zero-based IDs 0..N-1. Sort the unique excluded IDs into e and let M = N - len(e). Draw K = min(8, M) distinct ranks r uniformly without replacement from [0, M). Map each rank to an eligible ID with r + searchsorted(e - arange(len(e)), r, side='right'), then convert back to one-based IDs. Cache exclusion arrays per user; use a documented exact without-replacement sampler rather than materializing an entire catalog permutation for every target. If M = 0, mark that user's positions unusable in all matched configurations and report the count. Do not loop indefinitely or silently duplicate negatives. Within matched context comparisons, reuse identical negatives. For the baseline-loss cells, retain the supplied baseline objective and use the first eligible sampled negative where its contract requires one; disclose any resulting sampling difference from the unchanged reference.

Objective: for retained position t, use L_t = -s_pos + logsumexp([s_pos, s_neg_1, ..., s_neg_K]) at temperature 1.0. This is uncorrected (K+1)-way classification, distinct from K independent binary losses. It is intentionally not presented as a full-catalog likelihood estimator. Under uniform without-replacement sampling, negative inclusion probability is K/M; an importance estimate of the eligible negative partition weights each sampled exponential by M/K while the guaranteed positive keeps weight 1. Such correction does not cancel uniformly between positive and negative logits, and the finite-sample log-partition estimate remains biased. Excluding other training positives also changes the partition being estimated. Do not add proposal correction or a temperature sweep to the initial contrast; either requires a separately declared experiment. Keep raw neural scores at inference. Track scoring memory and GPU time because K negatives increase training cost.

Inference and serialization: prediction initially uses full available histories and the maximum index whose item ID is nonzero, never count-1. Preserve the baseline explicit empty-history behavior. Cropping changes training inputs, not inference policy, and creates a possible distribution mismatch. If supported by host diagnostic hooks and budget, evaluate each frozen compared model with both full and prespecified cropped histories, keeping users, targets and candidates fixed. These auxiliary interventions must not modify the official evaluator or silently become another selection sweep. Record the crop rule and report unavailable hooks explicitly. Store training configuration with each checkpoint. Update the embedded predictor writer whenever architecture, checkpoint format or inference behavior changes, and verify evaluation-mode feature and candidate-score parity after reconstruction. Each deployed category loads exactly one selected independently trained checkpoint and produces one neural score; no independent scorer, averaging or score fusion is allowed.

Define the catalog as sorted valid integer IDs 1 through view.model.itemnum. Freeze features once. First score every chunk and extract each target's score from its actual catalog chunk before eligibility masking. These are diagnostic tie bounds; do not infer the host tie rule. Maintain the ten highest eligible competitor scores to compute target-minus-tenth-competitor margin; mark it missing when fewer than ten alternatives exist. For competitor identities use descending score then ascending item ID consistently, rather than relying on torch.topk's tied-index ordering. Reject nonfinite features, target scores, or eligible competitor scores with counted reasons.

Validate streaming counters, exclusions, repeat handling, duplicate-event handling, and ties against materialized candidate scores for a small selected subset using the identical chunk computations. Include synthetic score-array checks for ties and fewer than ten alternatives without fitting additional models. A single full-matrix GEMM can produce slightly different scores; treat that comparison as a numerical-sensitivity check rather than an unquestioned reference. FP64 recomputation can diagnose near-tie sensitivity but cannot establish the original FP32 rank.

Report rank quantiles, normalized-rank bounds, training-event HR@10 bounds, target-minus-tenth-competitor margins, original supplied-negative margins, eligible-negative paired summaries, target frequencies, and distinct event/user counts. Compare supplied-negative win rates with catalog competition on the same eligible observations. Optional competitor IDs, scores, training frequencies, and top-10 popularity concentration are descriptive diagnostics. Unobserved competitors are not confirmed negatives, and popularity counts do not identify exposure propensities or dislikes. Aggregate categories with equal category weights only for explicitly named training diagnostics; never label them validation results.

If uncertainty is reported, use 2,000 user-cluster bootstrap replicates with local seed 42, retaining each sampled user's selected events together and recomputing the declared event-weighted statistic. Disclose that intervals condition on the selected events, checkpoint, candidate protocol, and numerical configuration; they exclude training-seed, adaptive-search, and stratified-event-sampling uncertainty. Do not claim simultaneous guarantees across strata or categories. With insufficient identifiable users, omit intervals and give a reason.

Training targets can be memorized, and popularity shortcuts can produce strong training ranks. This audit adds no learned shortcut itself, but adapting a model repeatedly to its outputs can overfit the search process. Do not optimize diagnostic scores as an objective. A later optional longitudinal extension may inspect three prespecified snapshots of the same training trajectory, without averaging their predictions or deploying multiple checkpoints; it is outside the initial bounded audit. Any training change must retain one jointly trained NextItNet model per category and be selected solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.

def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
    previous_mode = self.view.model.training
    metrics, definitions = {}, {}
    previous_precision = capture_precision_settings()
    try:
        self.view.model.eval()
        configure_recorded_fp32_audit_settings()
        # CUDA environment settings must already be configured before initialization.
        cached = cache_batches(train_loader, maximum=10)
        events = identify_training_events(cached, self.view.user_train)
        # Identity = (category, user_id, target_endpoint); reject ambiguous matches.
        events = deduplicate_event_identities(events)
        validate_strictly_preceding_contexts(events)
        frequency_bands = tied_quintile_bands_from_training_histories()
        events = stratified_sample_without_replacement(
            events, frequency_bands, length_bands=[5, 15, 31],
            maximum=128, local_seed=42,
            allocation='balanced_cells_then_fixed_order_redistribution')
        record_pool_sizes_selection_probabilities_and_exclusions()

        with torch.inference_mode():
            for batch in fixed_user_batches(events, size=16):
                last = largest_original_occupied_index(batch.sequence)
                validate_nonempty_sequences_and_aligned_targets(batch, last)
                features = gather_sequence_features(
                    self.view.log2feats(batch.sequence), last)
                chunks = fixed_sorted_catalog_chunks(
                    first_id=1, last_id=self.view.model.itemnum, width=4096)

                # Pass 1: target scores come from actual catalog scoring calls.
                target_scores = empty_target_score_vector(batch)
                for items in chunks:
                    scores = self.view.predict_score(features, items)
                    extract_target_scores_before_masking(
                        scores, items, batch.target, target_scores)
                mark_nonfinite_target_or_feature_rows()

                counters = initialize_per_protocol_counters()
                for items in chunks:
                    # Replay identical feature batch, shapes, order, and calls.
                    scores = self.view.predict_score(features, items)
                    for protocol in ['repeat_capable', 'unseen_target']:
                        event_eligible, item_eligible = eligibility(
                            protocol, items, batch.target,
                            complete_pre_target_history=batch.pre_target_history)
                        # Unseen protocol excludes repeat-target events entirely.
                        alternatives = item_eligible & (items != batch.target)
                        reject_nonfinite_eligible_rows_with_counts(scores)
                        counters[protocol].update(
                            greater=count(scores > target_scores, alternatives),
                            ties=count(scores == target_scores, alternatives),
                            eligible=count(item_eligible),
                            top10_competitors=stable_top10(
                                scores, items, alternatives,
                                ordering='score_desc_item_id_asc'))

                record_rank_bounds_and_tenth_competitor_margins(counters)
                record_repeat_and_first_time_strata()
                record_original_valid_distinct_supplied_negative_margins(batch)
                record_protocol_eligible_negative_comparisons(batch)
                record_frequency_length_event_and_user_counts(batch)

        validate_streaming_against_materialized_identical_chunk_scores(
            small_subset=True, include_ties_exclusions_and_repeat_cases=True)
        report_bounded_shape_sensitivity_checks_separately()
        summarize_selected_sample_with_explicit_event_weighting()
        optional_user_cluster_bootstrap(replicates=2000, local_seed=42)
        define_every_metric_population_filter_tie_rule_and_missing_reason()
    finally:
        restore_precision_settings(previous_precision)
        self.view.model.train(previous_mode)
    return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

code_difficulty.negative: Reliable event reconstruction, complete pre-target filtering, two-pass scoring, numerical checks, and aggregation make this more demanding than a basic catalog scan.

The proposed experiment is **target-matched suffix augmentation with multiple-negative training for the corrected NextItNet**. It targets broad relevance displacing specific recent matches and older interactions persisting despite coherent recent behavior. Improvement remains a hypothesis; neither failure establishes that historical context caused the recommendations.

**Insights and directions.** Three observations guide the starting point: (1) causal dilated convolutions preserve order but do not identify obsolete interests; (2) Electronics’ negative lower-tail margin (−0.2595) and 12.27% sampled ranking-error rate motivate better discrimination; (3) mapped cosine scores near 0.5 provide little evidence of directional collapse, although they cannot exclude low-dimensional representations. An embedding-diversity penalty therefore lacks current justification.

Literature suggests three directions. NextItNet already supervises historical positions [1]; suffix cropping consequently changes both context and target weighting unless controlled. Sampled-softmax research motivates several competing negatives, but eight-negative uncorrected classification is nine-way cross-entropy, not eight binary losses or an unbiased full-catalog objective [2,5]. Temporal augmentation motivates testing context usefulness [3], while CLA-Rec motivates text alignment without establishing benefits from corpus-only encoders [4]. Cropping research reports that adding cropping to sliding-window training can underperform sliding windows alone [6].

| Context selection | Target-matched suffix augmentation | Does context removal help beyond recency-weighted supervision? |
| Discrimination | Multiple-negative cross-entropy | Do sampled training margins translate to HR@10? |

    maxlen: int,

) -> dict[str, float]:

    if len(val_users) > num_users:
        rng = random.Random(SEED)
        val_users = rng.sample(val_users, num_users)

        return {"HR@10": 0.0, "HR@20": 0.0, "NDCG@10": 0.0, "NDCG@20": 0.0}

    hr10 = hr20 = ndcg10 = ndcg20 = 0.0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for user in val_users:
            target = user_valid[user][0]
            history = user_train[user]
            interacted = set(history) | {target, 0}
            candidates = [target]
            while len(candidates) < 100 and itemnum > 0:
                neg_item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
                if neg_item not in interacted:
                    interacted.add(neg_item)
                    candidates.append(neg_item)
            seq_t = _history_to_tensor(history, maxlen, device)
            cand_t = torch.tensor(candidates, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            scores = model.score_candidates(seq_t, cand_t).detach().cpu().tolist()
            rank = sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: -scores[i]).index(0)

class NextItNetBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self, hidden_units: int, dilation: int, kernel_size: int, dropout_rate: float
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.dilation = dilation
        self.kernel_size = kernel_size
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv1d(
            hidden_units, hidden_units, kernel_size, dilation=dilation, padding=0
        )
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv1d(
            hidden_units, hidden_units, kernel_size, dilation=dilation, padding=0
        )
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.activation = nn.GELU()

    def _causal_conv(self, conv: nn.Conv1d, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        pad = (self.kernel_size - 1) * self.dilation
        x = nn.functional.pad(x, (pad, 0))
        return conv(x)

    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Prevent padding leakage between causal convolutions
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        residual = x * mask
        y = (self.norm1(residual) * mask).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self._causal_conv(self.conv1, y).transpose(1, 2) * mask
        y = self.dropout(self.activation(y)) * mask
        y = (self.norm2(y) * mask).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self._causal_conv(self.conv2, y).transpose(1, 2) * mask
        return (residual + self.dropout(y)) * mask

    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END


class NextItNetModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self,
        itemnum: int,
        hidden_units: int = 64,
        num_blocks: int = 8,
        kernel_size: int = 3,
        dropout_rate: float = 0.2,
        maxlen: int = 128,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.itemnum = itemnum
        self.hidden_units = hidden_units
        self.maxlen = maxlen
        self.item_emb = nn.Embedding(itemnum + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos_emb = nn.Embedding(maxlen + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        dilations = [1, 2, 4, 8] * max(1, math.ceil(num_blocks / 4))
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [
                NextItNetBlock(hidden_units, dilations[i], kernel_size, dropout_rate)
                for i in range(num_blocks)
            ]
        )
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        with torch.no_grad():
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.item_emb.weight)
            self.item_emb.weight[0].zero_()
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.pos_emb.weight)
            self.pos_emb.weight[0].zero_()

    def encode_sequence(self, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch, length = seq.shape
        pos = torch.arange(length, device=seq.device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch, -1) + 1
        pos = pos * (seq != 0).long()
        x = self.item_emb(seq) * (self.hidden_units**0.5) + self.pos_emb(pos)
        ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Mask all temporal block boundaries and final features
        mask = (seq != 0).unsqueeze(-1).to(x.dtype)
        x = self.dropout(x) * mask
        for block in self.blocks:
            x = block(x, mask)
        return self.norm(x) * mask
        ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END

    def forward(self, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor):
        out = self.encode_sequence(seq)
        pos_scores = (out * self.item_emb(pos)).sum(dim=-1)
        neg_scores = (out * self.item_emb(neg)).sum(dim=-1)
        return pos_scores, neg_scores

    def score_candidates(
        self, seq: torch.Tensor, candidates: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        out = self.encode_sequence(seq)
        positions = torch.arange(seq.size(1), device=seq.device).expand_as(seq)
        last = positions.masked_fill(seq == 0, -1).max(dim=1).values.clamp(min=0)
        user_emb = out[0, last[0]]
        cand_emb = self.item_emb(candidates)
        return torch.matmul(cand_emb, user_emb)

class TargetMatchedSampler:
    def __init__(self, user_train, itemnum, dataset_name):
        self.itemnum = itemnum
        self.category_key = DEFAULT_DATASETS.index(dataset_name)

        self.exclusions = {}
        excluded_users = 0
        for user in sorted(user_train):
            history = user_train[user]
            if len(history) < 2:
                continue
            if any(i < 1 or i > itemnum for i in history):
                raise ValueError("Training history contains an invalid item ID")
            excluded = np.asarray(sorted(set(history)), dtype=np.int64) - 1
            eligible = itemnum - len(excluded)
            if eligible == 0:
                excluded_users += 1
                continue
            # Rank-to-ID thresholds for the complement of the training-item set.
            self.exclusions[user] = (excluded - np.arange(len(excluded)), eligible)
            self.users.append(user)
        if not self.users:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "No training users have both targets and eligible negatives"
            )
        print(
            f"  [{dataset_name}] negative_exhausted_users={excluded_users}", flush=True
        )

    @staticmethod
    def distinct_ranks(rng, population, count, size):
        if not (0 < count <= population) or size < 1:
            raise ValueError("Negative sampling requires positive valid dimensions")
        # Each target independently draws ordered uniform ranks without replacement.
        # At each step, map a uniform complement rank past earlier selected ranks.
        # Vectorize across targets; never allocate a catalog-sized permutation.
        ranks = np.empty((size, count), dtype=np.int64)
        for offset in range(count):
            draw = rng.integers(population - offset, size=size)
            if offset:
                thresholds = np.sort(ranks[:, :offset], axis=1)
                thresholds = thresholds - np.arange(offset, dtype=np.int64)
                draw = draw + (thresholds <= draw[:, None]).sum(axis=1)
            ranks[:, offset] = draw
        return ranks

    def batch(self, update, batch_size, maxlen, mode, receptive_field):

            np.random.default_rng(
                np.random.SeedSequence([SEED, self.category_key, update, stream])

            for stream in range(3)

        batch_rng, suffix_rng, negative_rng = streams
        seq = np.zeros((batch_size, maxlen), dtype=np.int64)
        pos = np.zeros_like(seq)
        retained = np.zeros_like(seq, dtype=bool)
        sampled_users = []
        removed_context = 0
        affected_targets = 0
        for row in range(batch_size):
            user = self.users[int(batch_rng.integers(len(self.users)))]
            sampled_users.append(user)
            history = self.histories[user]
            n = min(maxlen, len(history) - 1)
            start = maxlen - n
            seq[row, start:] = history[-n - 1 : -1]
            pos[row, start:] = history[-n:]
            kept = (
                n if suffix_rng.random() < 0.5 else int(suffix_rng.integers(1, n + 1))
            )
            boundary = maxlen - kept
            retained[row, boundary:] = True
            if mode.startswith("cropped"):
                # Positive targets keep their original positions and identities.
                for target_position in range(boundary, maxlen):
                    removed = max(
                        0, boundary - max(start, target_position - receptive_field + 1)
                    )
                    removed_context += removed
                    affected_targets += int(removed > 0)
                seq[row, :boundary] = 0

        negatives = np.zeros((len(rows), NEGATIVE_COUNT), dtype=np.int64)
        # np.nonzero returns row-major indices, so each row's targets are contiguous.
        # Batch their independent draws instead of executing Python once per target.
        target_counts = np.bincount(rows, minlength=batch_size)

            thresholds, eligible = self.exclusions[sampled_users[row]]
            k = min(NEGATIVE_COUNT, eligible)
            ranks = self.distinct_ranks(negative_rng, eligible, k, int(target_count))
            stop = first + int(target_count)
            negatives[first:stop, :k] = (
                ranks + np.searchsorted(thresholds, ranks, side="right") + 1
            )
            first = stop
        stats = {
            "retained_targets": int(len(rows)),
            "negative_draws": int(np.count_nonzero(negatives)),
            "affected_targets": affected_targets,
            "removed_context_positions": removed_context,
        }

def matched_sequence_loss(model, batch, device, mode):
    seq, pos, rows, columns, negatives, stats = batch
    seq_t = torch.as_tensor(seq, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    rows_t = torch.as_tensor(rows, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    columns_t = torch.as_tensor(columns, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    targets = torch.as_tensor(pos[rows, columns], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    negative_t = torch.as_tensor(negatives, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    features = model.encode_sequence(seq_t)[rows_t, columns_t]
    positive_scores = (features * model.item_emb(targets)).sum(-1)
    if mode.endswith("bpr"):
        negative_scores = (features * model.item_emb(negative_t[:, 0])).sum(-1)
        loss = nn.functional.softplus(negative_scores - positive_scores).mean()
    else:
        negative_scores = torch.einsum(
            "nd,nkd->nk", features, model.item_emb(negative_t)
        ).masked_fill(negative_t == 0, float("-inf"))
        logits = torch.cat((positive_scores[:, None], negative_scores), dim=1)
        # Uncorrected (K+1)-way classification at temperature one.
        loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(
            logits, torch.zeros(len(rows), dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        )
    return loss

        self, sample_size: int = 2048, seed: int = 42
    ):
        with torch.no_grad():
            emb = self.model.item_emb.weight.detach()
            emb = emb[
                1 : self.model.model.itemnum + 1
            ]  # exclude padding and reserved mask tokens

            n = emb.size(0)
            if n <= 2:
                return 0.0

            g = torch.Generator(device=emb.device)
            g.manual_seed(seed)

            k = min(sample_size, n)
            idx = torch.randperm(n, generator=g, device=emb.device)[:k]
            x = emb.index_select(0, idx)
            x = F.normalize(x, p=2, dim=-1)

            gram = x @ x.t()
            offdiag_sum = gram.sum() - gram.diag().sum()
            offdiag_cnt = k * (k - 1)

            assert singleton["normalized_rank_lower"] is None
            assert singleton["rank_upper"] == 1
            # Use more than ten alternatives to check tenth-score arithmetic.
            many_ids = np.arange(1, 13)
            many_scores = np.linspace(0.1, 1.2, 12, dtype=np.float32)
            many = rank_result(many_ids, many_scores, 1, many_scores[0])
            assert many["tenth_competitor_margin"] == (
                float(many_scores[0]) - float(many_scores[2])
            )
            assert len({("u", 3), ("u", 3), ("u", 4)}) == 2
            metrics["synthetic_checks_passed"] = True

            with torch.inference_mode(), torch.autocast(
                device_type=device.type, enabled=False
            ):
                for event_index, event in enumerate(selected):
                    sequence = event["sequence"][None, :]
                    feats = self.model.log2feats(sequence)
                    if (
                        not isinstance(feats, torch.Tensor)
                        or feats.ndim != 3
                        or tuple(feats.shape[:2]) != tuple(sequence.shape)
                    ):
                        raise ValueError(
                            "ModelView.log2feats must preserve B x L positions"
                        )
                    feature = feats[:, event["last"], :].detach()
                    if (
                        feature.dtype != torch.float32
                        or not torch.isfinite(feature).all()
                    ):
                        counts["invalid_feature_events"] += 1
                        continue
                    target, negative = event["target"], event["negative"]
                    valid_negative = 1 <= negative <= vocab and negative != target
                    if not valid_negative:
                        counts["invalid_supplied_negative_events"] += 1

                    def score_chunk(start):
                        ids = torch.arange(
                            start, min(start + width, vocab + 1), device=feature.device
                        )
                        result = self.model.predict_score(feature, ids)
                        # Singleton user batches avoid the host adapter's extra broadcasting axes.
                        if (
                            not isinstance(result, torch.Tensor)
                            or result.numel() != ids.numel()
                        ):
                            raise ValueError(
                                "ModelView catalog score shape is incompatible with singleton scoring"
                            )
                        if result.dtype != torch.float32:
                            raise ValueError("Catalog score dtype is not FP32")
                        return (
                            ids.cpu().numpy(),
                            result.reshape(-1).detach().cpu().numpy(),
                        )

                    target_score = None
                    negative_score = None
                    for start in range(1, vocab + 1, width):
                        ids, values = score_chunk(start)
                        if ids[0] <= target <= ids[-1]:
                            target_score = values[target - start]
                        if valid_negative and ids[0] <= negative <= ids[-1]:
                            negative_score = values[negative - start]
                    if target_score is None or not np.isfinite(target_score):
                        counts["nonfinite_target_events"] += 1
                        continue
                    # Subtract as Python floats to avoid FP32 overflow and to
                    # use identical arithmetic in streaming/reference margins.
                    margin = (
                        float(target_score) - float(negative_score)
                        if valid_negative
                        and negative_score is not None
                        and np.isfinite(negative_score)
                        else None
                    )
                    if valid_negative and margin is None:
                        counts["nonfinite_supplied_negative_events"] += 1
                    seen = set(event["history"])
                    seen_ids = np.asarray(sorted(seen), dtype=np.int64)
                    repeat = target in seen
                    # Preserve supplied-negative observations even when a later
                    # catalog numerical check excludes this event's ranks.
                    metrics.setdefault("original_supplied_negative_events", []).append(
                        {
                            "user": event["user"],
                            "target_endpoint": event["endpoint"],
                            "target": target,
                            "negative": negative,
                            "valid_distinct_negative": valid_negative,
                            "supplied_negative_margin": margin,
                            "repeat": repeat,
                            "repeat_capable_negative_eligible": valid_negative,
                            "unseen_target_negative_eligible": (
                                valid_negative and not repeat and negative not in seen
                            ),
                        }
                    )
                    counts["selected_repeat_events"] += int(repeat)
                    counts["unseen_protocol_excluded_repeat_events"] += int(repeat)
                    protocols = ["repeat_capable"] + (
                        [] if repeat else ["unseen_target"]
                    )
                    state = {
                        p: {
                            "n": 0,
                            "g": 0,
                            "t": 0,
                            "id_ties": 0,
                            "bad": False,
                            "top": [],
                        }
                        for p in protocols
                    }
                    materialized = []
                    replay_ok = True
                    for start in range(1, vocab + 1, width):
                        ids, values = score_chunk(start)
                        if ids[0] <= target <= ids[-1]:
                            replay_ok &= bool(values[target - start] == target_score)
                        if (
                            valid_negative
                            and ids[0] <= negative <= ids[-1]
                            and np.isfinite(negative_score)
                        ):
                            replay_ok &= bool(
                                values[negative - start] == negative_score
                            )
                        if event_index < 2:
                            materialized.append(values.copy())
                        for protocol, counter in state.items():
                            eligible = np.ones(len(ids), dtype=bool)
                            if protocol == "unseen_target":
                                eligible &= ~np.isin(ids, seen_ids)
                            counter["bad"] |= bool(
                                (~np.isfinite(values[eligible])).any()
                            )
                            counter["n"] += int(eligible.sum())
                            alternative = eligible & (ids != target)
                            a_ids, a_values = ids[alternative], values[alternative]
                            counter["g"] += int((a_values > target_score).sum())
                            counter["t"] += int((a_values == target_score).sum())
                            counter["id_ties"] += int(
                                ((a_values == target_score) & (a_ids < target)).sum()
                            )
                            finite = np.isfinite(a_values)
                            order = np.lexsort((a_ids[finite], -a_values[finite]))[:10]
                            new_top = [
                                (float(s), int(i))
                                for s, i in zip(
                                    a_values[finite][order], a_ids[finite][order]
                                )
                            ]
                            counter["top"] = sorted(
                                counter["top"] + new_top,
                                key=lambda pair: (-pair[0], pair[1]),
                            )[:10]
                    if not replay_ok:
                        counts["target_or_negative_replay_mismatch_events"] += 1
                        continue
                    for protocol, counter in state.items():
                        if counter["bad"]:
                            counts[protocol + ":nonfinite_eligible_score_events"] += 1
                            continue
                        n, g, t = counter["n"], counter["g"], counter["t"]
                        top = counter["top"]
                        row = {
                            "user": event["user"],
                            "target_endpoint": event["endpoint"],
                            "target": target,
                            "target_frequency": int(frequencies[target]),
                            "frequency_band": event["frequency_band"],
                            "length_band": event["length_band"],
                            "repeat": repeat,
                            "protocol": protocol,
                            "eligible_candidates": n,
                            "greater": g,
                            "ties": t,
                            "rank_lower": 1 + g,
                            "rank_upper": 1 + g + t,
                            "rank_id_ascending": 1 + g + counter["id_ties"],
                            "normalized_rank_lower": g / (n - 1) if n > 1 else None,
                            "normalized_rank_upper": (
                                (g + t) / (n - 1) if n > 1 else None
                            ),
                            "tenth_competitor_margin": (
                                float(target_score - top[9][0])
                                if len(top) == 10
                                else None
                            ),
                            "top_competitor_ids": [i for _, i in top],
                            "supplied_negative_margin": margin,
                            "negative_eligible": valid_negative
                            and (protocol == "repeat_capable" or negative not in seen),
                        }
                        if event_index < 2:
                            all_values = np.concatenate(materialized)
                            all_ids = np.arange(1, vocab + 1)
                            eligible = np.ones(vocab, dtype=bool)
                            if protocol == "unseen_target":
                                eligible &= ~np.isin(all_ids, seen_ids)
                            reference = rank_result(
                                all_ids[eligible],
                                all_values[eligible],
                                target,
                                target_score,
                            )
                            for name, value in reference.items():
                                assert row[name] == value, (
                                    "Streaming reference mismatch: " + name
                                )
                            counts["materialized_protocol_checks_passed"] += 1
                        records.append(row)
            if not selected:
                metrics["catalog_audit_missing_reason"] = (
                    "No uniquely identifiable eligible training events."
                )
            elif not records:
                metrics["catalog_audit_missing_reason"] = (
                    "No events passed numerical checks."
                )
            else:
                output = {}
                for protocol in ("repeat_capable", "unseen_target"):
                    rows = [r for r in records if r["protocol"] == protocol]
                    output[protocol] = {
                        "overall": summary(rows),
                        "repeat": summary([r for r in rows if r["repeat"]]),
                        "first_time": summary([r for r in rows if not r["repeat"]]),
                        "frequency_strata": {
                            str(f): summary(
                                [r for r in rows if r["frequency_band"] == f]
                            )
                            for f in range(5)
                        },
                        "length_strata": {
                            str(l): summary([r for r in rows if r["length_band"] == l])
                            for l in range(4)
                        },
                    }
                metrics["catalog_audit"] = output
            metrics["events"] = records
            metrics["sampling_cells"] = allocation
            metrics["target_frequency_quintile_boundaries"] = thresholds.tolist()
            metrics["catalog_frequency_bin_sizes"] = {
                str(f): int((bands[1:] == f).sum()) for f in range(5)
            }
            metrics["length_band_labels"] = ["1-5", "6-15", "16-31", "32+"]
            metrics["synthetic_checks_passed"] = True
        except RuntimeError as error:
            # Only a specifically identified deterministic-operation failure is
            # an unavailable audit. Propagate OOM, shape and other runtime bugs.
            message = str(error)
            deterministic_failure = "deterministic" in message.lower() and (
                "implementation" in message.lower()
                or "CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG" in message
            )
            if not deterministic_failure:
                raise
            import warnings

            warnings.warn(
                "Catalog audit unavailable under deterministic FP32 settings: "
                + message,
                RuntimeWarning,
            )
            metrics["catalog_audit"] = None
            metrics["events"] = []
            metrics["catalog_audit_missing_reason"] = message
            metrics["partial_catalog_results_discarded"] = True
        finally:
            for module, mode in modes:
                module.training = mode
            torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = previous["matmul_tf32"]
            torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = previous["cudnn_tf32"]
            torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = previous["benchmark"]
            torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = previous["cudnn_deterministic"]
            torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(
                previous["deterministic"], warn_only=previous["warn_only"]
            )
            random.setstate(python_state)
            np.random.set_state(numpy_state)
            torch.random.set_rng_state(torch_state)
            if cuda_state is not None:
                torch.cuda.set_rng_state_all(cuda_state)
            metrics["counts"] = dict(counts)
            metrics["elapsed_diagnostic_seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - started
        return {"metrics": metrics, "metric_definitions": definitions}
